title: Selbu-style mittens
subtitle: Full mittens with an eight-pointed star in two-colour stranded colourwork.
excerpt: Full mittens with a traditional eight-pointed star motif in two-colour stranded colourwork, worked in the round in DK wool. Afterthought thumb. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
sourceNotes: The eight-pointed Selbu star is the central motif of the Selbu mitten tradition from Selbu, Norway. Traditional Selbu patterns entered the public domain through the Husfliden collections of the late 19th century. The star motif itself is a folk pattern predating copyright; the specific chart here is an original arrangement.

knitting.gaugeText: 24 sts × 28 rounds = 10 × 10 cm in two-colour stranded stocking stitch on 3.75 mm needles, blocked.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Hand circumference 18 (20, 22) cm with 1 to 2 cm negative ease.

glossaryTerms.definition: A technique where two or more yarn colours are carried across each round, with the unused colour floating as a strand (float) on the wrong side of the fabric. Both colours are picked up and set down as needed to form the pattern. Keeping floats short and even prevents the fabric from puckering.

A thumb opening made by working the thumb stitches in waste yarn during the hand, then returning to them after the hand is complete. The waste yarn is removed to reveal live stitches which are picked up and worked as the thumb.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

content.text: Full mittens with a traditional Selbu eight-pointed star in
stranded colourwork
, worked in the round in DK wool, sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
The construction is seamless, worked in the round using
magic loop

on a long circular. The colourwork gauge is slightly tighter than single-colour stocking stitch at the same needle size because the floats pull the fabric in. Cast on 2 extra stitches per 10 cm of expected circumference to compensate, then block firmly after finishing. The star motif sits on the back of the hand. The thumb uses the
afterthought thumb
method. Budget about 70 g of main colour and 40 g of contrast colour (each about 155 m / 170 yards) per pair.
What you need

items.name: Yarn MC (main colour)
items.qty: 70 g (about 155 m / 170 yards) DK-weight wool, traditionally white or cream

items.name: Yarn CC (contrast colour)
items.qty: 40 g (about 90 m / 100 yards) DK-weight wool, traditionally black or dark blue

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3.75 mm (UK 9 / US 5) circular needle, at least 80 cm cable, for magic loop

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 2: 1 for the beginning of the round, 1 for the thumb position

items.name: Waste yarn
items.qty: About 30 cm of smooth contrasting yarn for the afterthought thumb

content.text: Gauge

24 stitches and 28 rounds to 10 cm in two-colour stranded stocking stitch on 3.75 mm needles, blocked. Colourwork gauge is tighter than single-colour gauge at the same needle size. Swatch in two colours before casting on. If your two-colour swatch gives 22 stitches per 10 cm rather than 24, move down one needle size.
Star motif chart

The chart below is 24 stitches wide and 24 rounds tall. It repeats once around the back of the hand. Work the chart reading right to left for every round (working in the round, all rounds are right-side rounds).

items.name: Rounds 1-3
items.qty: MC border: knit all stitches in MC

items.name: Rounds 4-21
items.qty: Star motif: follow the 18-round star chart (see below)

items.name: Rounds 22-24
items.qty: MC border: knit all stitches in MC

Pattern
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count and measurement reads S (M, L).
Cast on and cuff

Using MC and the long-tail cast-on, cast on 40 (44, 48) stitches. These are 2 stitches more per size than single-colour mittens to compensate for colourwork gauge. Join to work in the round. Work 2×2 rib in MC for 24 (26, 28) rounds.
Colourwork body

Switch to stocking stitch. Work 3 rounds in MC. On the next round, begin the star chart: the first 24 stitches (back of hand) follow the chart; the remaining 16 (20, 24) stitches (palm) are worked in MC throughout. Carry CC up the palm inside, catching it every few rounds.
Thumb marker
At round 12 of the chart (midpoint), mark the thumb on the palm: knit the first 9 (10, 11) palm stitches with waste yarn, slip back and re-knit with MC. Continue the chart round to end.
Complete the chart and close the top

Complete chart rounds 13-24. Work 2 more plain rounds in MC. Place 4 decrease markers evenly and work the mitten top: (k1, ssk, knit to 3 before marker, k2tog, k1) 4 times, with 1 plain round between decrease rounds, until 8 stitches remain. Draw yarn through and close.
Thumb
Remove waste yarn and pick up 9 (10, 11) stitches above and below. Work 12 (14, 14) rounds in MC stocking stitch. Decrease round: (k1, k2tog) across. Close.
Common faults
Floats pulled too tight: the fabric is puckered and the mitten is too narrow. Spread the stitches along the right needle before dropping the float, and do not pull the float taut.
Floats too long on the palm: the palm stitches are all in one colour for several rounds. Twist the unused colour around the working colour every 4 stitches to lock it in place.

Star misshapen after blocking: the floats varied in tension across different rounds. Wet-block firmly by stretching the mitten to the stated measurement and pinning the star points square before drying.
Finishing
Weave in all tails on the wrong side. Wet-block and pin to shape, stretching the star to its correct proportions. Dry flat.
Care
Hand wash in cool water with a wool-safe detergent. Re-block to shape each time for best results.
What to try next

From here, the natural next step is a traditional Selbu mitten with a full colourwork cuff, side border, and thumb gusset all in pattern. The thumb in a Selbu mitten traditionally matches the main body motif rather than being worked plain.
